concepts.title: Magma Melts Deep Underground
concepts.explanation: In some places deep inside the Earth, it is hot enough to melt rock. This melted rock is called magma. Magma is lighter for its size than the solid rock around it, so it slowly rises. It collects in a big pool under the ground called a magma chamber.
concepts.example: Think of a bubble in a bath. It floats up because it is lighter than the water around it. Magma rises in a similar way.

concepts.title: Eruptions and the Parts of a Volcano
concepts.explanation: Magma holds gas, like the bubbles in soda. When enough gas and magma push up, they burst out. This is an eruption. The magma travels up a tube called the vent. It comes out of a bowl-shaped opening at the top, called the crater. Once magma reaches the surface, we call it lava. Lava cools and hardens into new rock.
concepts.example: Think of what happens when a shaken soda is opened: the fizz shoots out the top. A volcano erupts in a similar way, but with hot melted rock.

concepts.title: Different Kinds of Volcanoes
concepts.explanation: Volcanoes come in different shapes. Shield volcanoes are wide with gentle slopes. Their runny lava flows far and builds them slowly. Cinder cones are small and steep, made of bits of rock that pile up. Composite volcanoes are tall and pointy. They are built from layers of lava and ash, and they can erupt with a big blast.
concepts.example: The volcanoes of Hawaii are shield volcanoes. Mount Fuji in Japan is a tall, pointy composite volcano.

diagram.alt_text: A cut-away picture of a volcano. Magma in a magma chamber deep underground rises up a tube called the vent, comes out of the crater at the top as lava flowing down the side, and a cloud of ash and gas rises into the sky.
diagram.caption: Magma rises up the vent and bursts out of the crater. At the surface, it is called lava!

questions.question: What do we call melted rock that is still deep under the ground?
questions.why: Melted rock is called magma while it is still underground.

questions.question: Why does magma slowly rise up toward the surface?
options: It is lighter than the solid rock around it
It is heavier than the rock around it
questions.why: Like a bubble in a bath, magma floats up because it is lighter.

questions.question: Magma reaches the surface and flows out. What do we call it now?
questions.why: Once magma reaches the surface, we call it lava.

questions.question: What is the tube that magma travels up inside a volcano?
questions.why: Magma travels up the vent and comes out of the crater at the top.

questions.question: A volcano is wide with gentle slopes, and its runny lava flows far. What kind is it?
questions.why: Shield volcanoes, like the ones in Hawaii, are wide with gentle slopes.

meta.scope_note: Cover what volcanoes are, how magma from deep inside the Earth rises and erupts as lava, the main parts of a volcano, and a few well-known kinds of volcanoes, explained simply for a fourth grader.
